subject: Initial fleet projection & sizing intake — Skylark Studios
summary: Pre-sales intake thread to capture Skylark Studios traffic profile and prompt/response characteristics to produce a dedicated GPU fleet projection. Includes traffic snapshot and next steps for a sizing workshop.
messages:
From: Anna Patel <anna@skylark.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Fleet projection intake — Skylark Studios

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks for taking this on. Were preparing to move two production features (assistant chat and automated content tagging) to a dedicated Redwood fleet and want a first-pass projection of what we should commit to. Attached is a short traffic snapshot and representative prompt samples. High-level context: were a mid-stage gaming studio with ~1.2M monthly DAU; these features are gated to logged-in users and a subset of advanced users.

Quick asks we hope you can confirm for the kickoff:
- A rough GPU pool size (number and type) to support our expected concurrency/peaks
- Latency SLOs vs cost tradeoffs (95th/99th)
- Whether caching/prefix-KV will meaningfully reduce commit needs for chat
- Any constraints for private deployment (VPC) vs hosted dedicated

Attached: skylark-traffic-snapshot.csv, skylark-prompt-samples.txt

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Patel
Head of AI Platforms | Skylark Studios
anna@skylark.ai | +1 415-555-0123

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Patel <anna@skylark.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 16:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fleet projection intake — Skylark Studios

Anna — thanks for the snapshot, this is exactly the sort of data that helps. I attached our quick sizing template (redwood-sizing-template.xlsx) to keep answers structured. Before I work up a projection, a couple clarifying questions that materially change the sizing: 

1) Concurrency model: what do you expect for sustained concurrency vs peak concurrency? Example: steady 400 concurrent tokens/sec across the fleet, peak 2x over a 5-10 minute window.
2) Prompt/response token distribution: the sample file helps, but can you confirm median and 95th token lengths for prompt and response? (sample suggests median prompt ~80 tokens, median response ~220 tokens)
3) Burst profile: are bursts seasonal, daily (e.g., morning launches), or correlated to in-game events? How fast do bursts ramp (seconds vs minutes)?
4) Required latency SLO: what are your target p50/p95/p99 for interactive chat and for async tagging?
5) Model variants: will you need both a high-quality (e.g., 70B fp16/H100) model and a lower-cost quantized variant for retries/fallbacks?
6) KV reuse: do you expect long conversational sessions where KV caching will yield large cache hits (reduces work per request)?
7) Compliance: is SOC2/PPI retention required on the private deployment?

If you can fill the template and answer these inline, Ill put together a baseline fleet projection and a few cost/perf tradeoff options. Proposed next step: 60-minute sizing workshop where we walk through traffic patterns and run a micro-sim to produce recommended GPU counts/configs. I can book time after I get the template back.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Anna Patel <anna@skylark.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mike Reynolds <mike@skylark.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fleet projection intake — Skylark Studios

On Wed, Jun 30, 2027 at 4:21 PM karthik_iyer@redwood.ai wrote:
> Anna — thanks for the snapshot, this is exactly the sort of data that helps. I attached our quick sizing template ...

Thanks Karthik — filled out the key fields in the attached CSV (skylark-traffic-snapshot.csv) and included representative prompt samples in skylark-prompt-samples.txt. Answers inline below: 

1) Concurrency: steady-state expected ~300 concurrent inference contexts for chat (average typing/think time accounted for). Typical daily peak ~900 concurrent (3x steady) for 6-12 minute windows during event drops.

2) Tokens: median prompt 75, 95th prompt 260. Median response 190, 95th response 640. Tagging pipeline is mostly short (prompt ~25, response ~40).

3) Burst profile: event-triggered bursts; ramp-up typically 2-5 minutes, not instantaneous. Some spikes from nightly leaderboard resets (short <2 min).

4) Latency SLOs: chat p50 < 120ms, p95 < 420ms, p99 < 900ms. Tagging can be softer: p95 < 1500ms.

5) Model strategy: primary is a 34B dense model for high-quality chat; fallback quantized 34B/int8 for cost-sensitive routes. We may pilot a smaller 13B for strictly tagging.

6) KV reuse: yes, typical session length of 8-12 messages with good reuse for quick continuations (we expect >60% cache hit for short-term sessions).

7) Compliance: we need SOC2 evidence; for now hosted dedicated is preferred but we may require private VPC later in the contract window.

Hope that helps — attaching CSV and prompt samples. Happy to hop on the workshop.

— Anna
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anna Patel <anna@skylark.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 10:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fleet projection intake — Skylark Studios

Looping in ops guidance and a couple quick ideas based on the numbers Anna provided.

- Baseline assumption: conversational workload dominated by 34B with median response ~190 tokens. With 300 steady concurrency and peaking to 900, conservative baseline for H100-class nodes (large memory, high throughput) is ~8-12 H100 GPUs to hit p95 targets with modest batching. If youre open to mixed fleet (H100 + A100p4 or triton bins), we can reduce H100 count by shifting less latency-sensitive tagging to cheaper GPUs.

- KV caching will reduce steady compute by ~25-40% depending on session length; ensure we enable prefix cache and tuned cache TTLs in the policy. That can materially lower committed capacity for the steady state but plan for peak headroom.

- Quantized fallback (int8) is an effective cost lever. Recommend policy: normal traffic -> fp16 34B; if latency budget tight or concurrency elevates, route tail requests to int8 34B with slightly higher diversity timeout. Also keep a smaller 13B for tagging-only routes to avoid wasting large model cycles.

- Batching: recommend continuous batching window tuned to 20-40ms for chat to balance p95 latency. We should simulate with your ramp profiles; continuous batching will significantly affect GPU saturation and therefore GPU counts.

I can draft two projection scenarios: (A) performance-first (p95 <420ms) and (B) cost-balanced (mix of quantized nodes + smaller models).

— Ben Carter
Principal Infrastructure Solutions Eng | Redwood Inference
